solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: US composer's dance music

parts.note: Samuel Barber was an American composer; his possessive gives these letters
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A query about an American composer's dance tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbershop is a style of close-harmony unaccompanied singing, so it is a genre of music.

clue.text: Lend something one lends, article replacing one

indicators.note: the article takes the place of the numeral in the word

parts.note: counsel is something given or lent to another person
one is the Roman numeral I
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An instruction to loan an item, with grammar fussing about articles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' swaps the I of ADVICE for AN.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance money is to lend it, as a loan ahead of time.

clue.text: Something to beat? Good try!

parts.note: bon is French for good
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: Encouragement to a competitor trying to beat a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' suggests defeating, but here it means striking a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A bongo is a small hand drum, an object struck to make rhythm.

clue.text: One or two girls?

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name, the first of the pair
Mary is a girl's name, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: A puzzled count of how many girls there are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is the definition: a single girl's name, which the question mark says may be read as two names joined.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a single feminine first name, so one girl can carry it.

clue.text: Old rebel in present custody, cut during capture

parts.note: being here is being present
a ward is someone in custody or care

indicators.note: the cutting word goes in the middle of the capturing word

parts.note: to take is to capture
to hew is to cut with an axe

explanation.surface: A former rebel, now jailed, was wounded while being caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in present' gives HERE, being present here. Hereward led an Anglo-Saxon revolt in the Fens after 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereward the Wake led English resistance against the Norman conquest in the Fens.

clue.text: Seen through window, a victory dance

indicators.note: items seen through glass sit within it, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: a pane is a sheet of window glass

explanation.surface: Someone glimpses a victory dance through a window.
explanation.definitionFit: The pavane is a slow, stately court dance of the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Game's ending, partner!

definitions.meaning: checkmate, the end of a chess game, often shortened
a friend or spouse, as in a pal or companion

explanation.surface: Someone announces the end of a game to a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the winning move is called this, and the same word is a casual term for a friend or spouse.

clue.text: Dash missing, un-twisted?

indicators.note: twisted means the letters are wound into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer worries that a punctuation mark has been left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' rearranges the letters of MISSING plus UN.
explanation.definitionFit: The short horizontal stroke used in arithmetic looks like a dash.

clue.text: Prepare to shoot at Mike, a revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned about, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebel readies a gun at a man named Mike.
explanation.definitionFit: Before firing, a shooter lines up the sights on a target.

clue.text: Banker, star in decline

indicators.note: something in decline goes backwards, so the star's word is read from right to left

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A financier who was once a star is now going downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is a crossword favourite for a river, something that has banks. The Avon is a river in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A river has banks, so the crossword joke makes any river a banker.

clue.text: Composer very partial to music — heavens above!

indicators.note: read cryptically, very is put inside the music, as if taken in by it

parts.note: a strain is a passage of music or melody
the heavens above us are the sky

explanation.surface: A composer who loves music cries out in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partial to' looks like fondness, but works as a container: very sits within the music.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor Stravinsky was the Russian-born composer of The Rite of Spring.

clue.text: Communicate, attending class

parts.note: to be in is to be present or attending
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: A pupil talks while sitting in a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a year group or class is called a form.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell or pass information on is to communicate it.

clue.text: Width of rails, for example?

parts.note: rails are marsh birds, so the width in question is the span across a bird's outstretched wings, not a railway gauge

explanation.surface: A question about the gauge of a railway track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rails' suggests railway lines, but a rail is also a wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The distance from tip to tip of a bird's extended wings measures its width in flight.

clue.text: Sailor miles away, prophet assumes

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so the prophet takes the distance inside

parts.note: a seer is one who foresees the future
far off, at a great distance

explanation.surface: A seer supposes a sailor is far from home.
explanation.definitionFit: One who travels by sea is a sailor or mariner.

clue.text: Slippery character in Marseille, say, working alone?

indicators.note: the slippery creature goes inside the country's name

parts.note: Marseille is a French city, standing for its country
an eel is notoriously slippery

explanation.surface: A shifty figure in Marseille operating on their own.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-employed worker who takes jobs independently works alone, without an employer.

clue.text: Leg perhaps, but not head, carrying a foot

indicators.note: the shortened limb carries the article inside it
the head means the first letter, which is dropped from the limb

parts.note: a leg is an example of a limb

explanation.surface: A leg, lacking a head, bears a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not head' drops L, leaving IMB, which then holds A.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry a metrical foot of a short then a long syllable is this unit.

clue.text: Terribly fragile democrat, US president

indicators.note: terribly suggests disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A frail Democrat is called an American president.
explanation.definitionFit: James Garfield was the twentieth president of the United States.

clue.text: End of enormous weed — this about a foot?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: to hoe is to weed with a garden tool

explanation.surface: Someone notices a huge weed wrapped round a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear goes around the foot, which the question mark hints at.

clue.text: Dog that can fly?

definitions.meaning: a hound bred for hunting hares
a bird of prey, or the British jump jet

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a flying dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A hare-hunting hound shares its name with a hawk and a vertical take-off jet.

clue.text: Opener in team coming down for practice

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

parts.note: rain that is coming down is falling, as weather

explanation.surface: A team's opening batsman comes out to practise as rain falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Training is practice undertaken to build a skill.

clue.text: Antiperspirant redundant? That's not a problem

definitions.meaning: if there is no perspiration, a deodorant is unnecessary
an informal reply meaning easily done

explanation.surface: An unneeded deodorant is shrugged off as no bother.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal way of saying something is easy and causes no trouble.

clue.text: Call coming from flier on fire, calm down!

parts.note: a coo is the call of a dove or pigeon
something lit is burning

explanation.surface: A bird on fire cries out and is told to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a slang command to relax and stop being agitated.

clue.text: Author an old pro, might you say?

indicators.note: signals that the word is said aloud, matching the writer's surname in sound

parts.note: an old-fashioned word for a prostitute or loose woman is trollop

explanation.surface: Someone calls a veteran writer an experienced professional.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope was the Victorian novelist of the Barsetshire books.

clue.text: Swimmers boxing in the end

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so the swimmers go around the little word

parts.note: fish are creatures that swim

explanation.surface: Fish caught in a box at the conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A finish is the close or conclusion of something.

clue.text: One's contemplated uniting part of church and council, finally

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Church and council come together for contemplation.
explanation.walkthrough: Navel-gazing means self-absorbed contemplation, which makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Mystics are said to contemplate the belly button, hence navel-gazing.

clue.text: Cook can see milk as sweet food

indicators.note: to cook the books is to falsify, so cook signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe step: a cook spots milk to make something sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: A simnel cake is a British fruitcake topped with marzipan, eaten around Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: This rich fruitcake is a sweet thing to eat.

clue.text: Wife goes on to contend opinion

indicators.note: the wife's letter is placed onto the end of the other piece

parts.note: to vie is to compete or contend

explanation.surface: A wife goes on to argue her point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a personal opinion or outlook.

clue.text: Bird golden retriever bites back

indicators.note: the letters found are read backwards
the phrase takes a bite out of its own letters, so the answer lies within

explanation.surface: A golden retriever snaps at a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the sea eagle, a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Surveying equipment, the tool I'd possibly use in the end

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be rearranged into another order
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A surveyor says which instrument they'd eventually pick up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges THETOOLID into THEODOLIT, then 'in the end' adds the final E of 'use'.
explanation.definitionFit: A theodolite is a surveyor's instrument for measuring angles.
